text: Alice proposed PostgreSQL for the payments platform during the architecture discussion.
Bob questioned whether PostgreSQL could handle the payments platform's projected transaction load.
Alice said the available benchmark results were inconclusive and asked the team to test PostgreSQL under peak load.
Carol reported that Redis was already being used for session caching in the payments platform.
Bob proposed using Redis for rate limiting, but it was unclear whether the proposal applied to the payments platform or to a separate service.
Alice reported that the PostgreSQL peak-load benchmark completed successfully, although its failover behavior remained uncertain.
Bob said the rate-limiting change might require a different deployment plan.
Carol said the payments platform team planned to keep Redis for caching while deciding on the database changes.
Alice proposed PostgreSQL again after the failover test, but no final adoption decision was recorded.
Bob and Carol reviewed the architecture document; Bob favored a separate rate-limiting service, while Carol favored keeping Redis for caching.
